exclusions.reason: The server test projects (Weir.Core.Tests, Weir.Infrastructure.Tests, Weir.Api.Tests, Weir.E2E.Tests) hold tests, which do not ship; counting them would make the figure move with the tests instead of the product.
The child process some tests start as a stand-in for a long-running program; it is test support and does not ship.
The contract suite and its fake tools judge a running server from outside; they are test code and do not ship. The server code they run is counted in the out-of-process figure.
Code marked as generated (source generators such as the one behind GeneratedRegex) is written by a tool; the hand-written code that calls it is what the tests cover.
The compiler writes closures, state machines and record members; their branches belong to the hand-written code they were made from, which is counted.

exclusions.provedBy: scripts/scenarios-ci/tray-menu.mjs, which chooses Copy address, Open data folder, Open logs folder and Report a problem on the real tray and reads the clipboard, File Explorer and the browser; the tray scenarios end the loop through Quit
exclusions.reason: Five one-line calls into Windows: start a program or open a folder or an address (Process.Start), put text on the clipboard, run the message loop, and end the thread's or the application's message loop. A unit test cannot answer them: they would open File Explorer and a browser on the machine, replace the person's clipboard, or block on a message loop that nothing ends. The tray's shell takes them as ShellEffects, so every line around them is run with recorders in WindowsTrayShellTests and TrayAppTests.

exclusions.provedBy: scripts/scenarios-ci/tray-menu.mjs and the install scenarios in scripts/scenarios-ci/windows-install.mjs, which answer the question on the real desktop and read the Run key
exclusions.reason: AskInMessageBox shows the modal question "Start Weir when you sign in to Windows?" and waits for a click; a unit test has nobody to answer it. Everything that decides whether to ask, and what the answer does, is run with a recorder in StartWithWindowsTests and TrayControllerStartTests.

exclusions.provedBy: scripts/scenarios-ci/tray-network.mjs, which chooses Change port, types a port into the real window and closes it without choosing
exclusions.reason: PortDialog.Ask opens the port window modally with ShowDialog and returns what the person chose; a unit test has nobody to close it. The window itself, its two options and its validation are run directly in PortDialogTests, and the controller takes the question as a function in TrayControllerMenuTests.
